samples.summary: `leaving()` compares a basename-joined destination against a basename-stripped current location, so under a non-"/" VITE_FRONTEND_BASENAME every guarded navigation (including same-document query rewrites) is treated as leaving
samples.evidence: `pathOf(navigator, to)` delegates to `history.createHref`, which does NOT prepend the router basename (react-router's `Router` only joins the basename inside `useNavigate`: it calls `navigator.push(joinPaths([basename, path.pathname]))`). The current location comes from `useLocation()`, which is basename-STRIPPED. So with basename `/wafflebase`, `pathOf(base, to)` = `/wafflebase/s/doc-1` while `pathOf(base, locationRef.current)` = `/s/doc-1`, and `next !== current` is always true. Non-"/" basenames are a supported, documented deployment: packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:381 ("Only if not served at /") and .github/workflows/publish-ghpage.yml:167 (`VITE_FRONTEND_BASENAME: ${{ vars.VITE_FRONTEND_BASENAME || '/' }}`). The doc comment on `pathOf` claims "basename included" for both sides; only the tests' MemoryRouter (basename "/") exercises the equal case, which is why the suite is green. Fix belongs in the new code (strip the basename from `to`, or compare against `base.createHref(locationRef.current)` after joining the basename).

samples.summary: The editors' "Document not found" automatic redirects are now interceptable by the new guard, and if the user picks Stay the redirect is cancelled permanently (the effect never re-fires)
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-detail.tsx:159-166 runs `navigate(fallbackSlug ? \`/w/${fallbackSlug}\` : "/documents", { replace: true })` inside a `useEffect` while the same component still renders `<SiteHeader ... syncStatus>` (docs-detail.tsx:196-200), i.e. while `SyncStatusChip` has a guard registered. The patched `navigator.replace` now holds that redirect behind the "Leave without saving?" dialog; clicking Stay drops `pendingRef` and the effect's deps (`isDocumentError`, `navigate`, `fallbackSlug`) do not change, so the redirect never happens again and the user is left inside a document the server reports as missing. Same pattern at packages/frontend/src/app/documents/document-detail.tsx:229, packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:183, packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-detail.tsx:161, packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-detail.tsx:125 — none of these call sites were updated to opt out of the guard.

samples.summary: Route changes that do not go through the react-router navigator bypass the new guard (browser back/forward, and full-page redirects via window.location)
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:30 sets `window.location.href = path` (session-expiry / login redirect), which never reaches the patched `navigator` — it falls back to the older `beforeunload` guard, which browsers suppress without prior interaction. Browser back/forward likewise arrives on the history listener, not the navigator; this is acknowledged in the new file (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:52) and docs/design/sync-status.md:299, so it is a known narrowing rather than a closure, but it is a reachable path out of an editor with stranded edits that shows no prompt.

samples.summary: PDF collab surfaces mount no SyncStatusChip, so the new navigation guard covers no PDF comment/presence edits either — the coverage claim "the five editable editors plus share-link editors" leaves this document type unguarded
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:734-745 deliberately renders no `SharedHeaderStatus` for `SharedPdfLayout` (and the owned route packages/frontend/src/app/files/file-shell.tsx mounts no DocumentProvider at all), so `useNavigationGuard` is never registered there even though a `DocumentProvider` carrying comment edits is mounted. Pre-existing and documented as out of scope for the chip, but the new guard inherits the gap silently: navigating away from a shared PDF with unsent comment changes still discards them with nothing said.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. `pathOf` (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:40-42) uses `navigator.createHref`, and `leaving` (:99-102) compares that against `pathOf(base, locationRef.current)` where the location comes from `useLocation()` (:67-71). The app mounts a non-data `BrowserRouter` with a configurable basename (App.tsx:1, App.tsx:95) and places the provider directly inside it (App.tsx:100). With react-router v7's non-data router, the navigator is the raw history object whose `createHref` does not prepend the basename, while `useNavigate` joins the basename onto the pathname before calling `navigator.push`/`replace` (:132-135) and `Router` strips the basename from the location `useLocation()` returns. Under a non-"/" basename the two sides therefore live in different path spaces and `leaving()` is always true, defeating the same-document exemption for query-only rewrites (a reachable case, e.g. workspace-documents.tsx:77 via `setSearchParams`). Non-"/" basenames are a supported, documented deployment (self-hosting.md:381; publish-ghpage.yml:167), and nothing in the repo normalises or restricts the basename. The only tests use a basename-less MemoryRouter (navigation-guard.test.tsx:58,114-120), so the suite does not refute it. No guard elsewhere makes the mismatch unreachable; the defect arises from an assumption about router configuration outside the diff, which fits this lens.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described. NavigationGuardProvider patches `navigator.replace` through `attempt()` (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:132-136, 104-116), which prompts for any path-changing navigation while a guard is registered, and `stay()` (lines 141-144) drops `pendingRef` without replaying or signalling the caller. `useNavigationGuard` (use-navigation-guard.ts:46-58) offers no opt-out. The provider wraps all editor routes (App.tsx:100-179, routes at 170-175), and SiteHeader renders SyncStatusChip whenever `syncStatus` is set (site-header.tsx:108), which registers the "Leave without saving?" guard (sync-status-chip.tsx:115-131). The redirect effects exist verbatim at docs-detail.tsx:159-166 (with `SiteHeader ... syncStatus` still rendered at 196-200 on the error path), document-detail.tsx:226-233, notes-detail.tsx:180-187, board-detail.tsx:122-129, each with deps [isDocumentError, navigate, fallbackSlug] that do not change after "Stay", so the redirect never re-fires. The path is reachable because the document query uses retry:false with react-query background refetching, so isError can flip after the user has unsent edits. (slides-detail.tsx:158-165 is weaker since :177 returns null on error, probably unmounting the chip first, but the other four stand.) This is a contract change to a shared symbol breaking call sites outside the diff — squarely in the blast-radius lane. No refutation ground applies.
